reviewMethod: Complete line-by-line semantic review of five Batch 1 operational workflow and production supply-chain authority files, including trigger coverage, exact-head checkout, permission scope, action pinning, release dependencies, vulnerability enforcement, recovery evidence, immutable identity propagation, failure behavior and permanent negative-test coverage.

residualRisks.statement: This bounded slice reviews five repository-supply-chain files only; every other Batch 1 path retains its pending status and no repository-wide completion claim is made.
Container rollback and volume-restore evidence is produced in ephemeral GitHub runners; recurring staging and production-host recovery activation remains governed by the operational rollout issues.
The public Browser Golden Path now runs for every pull request and main push, but its scenario set remains a bounded public-route contract rather than exhaustive product behavior coverage.

reviewNotes: Triggers, read-only default permissions, exact-head checkout, governed policy tests, Compose input validation, immutable build identity, rootless runtime inspection, SBOM generation, vulnerability gating, recovery jobs, publication permissions, digest signing and evidence retention were reviewed as one release sequence.
Publication now requires both the verification and recovery jobs, and the Trivy gate rejects HIGH or CRITICAL findings even when no upstream fix is currently available.

findings.attackPath: A push to main could publish, attest and sign an immutable production image after artifact verification while the rollback or persistent-volume recovery job had failed.
findings.affectedInvariant: No production image may be published unless both artifact verification and recovery evidence succeed for the same release workflow.
findings.evidence: The former publish job declared needs: verify only; the remediated job declares the exact dependency set [verify, recovery].
findings.verificationRequirement: The permanent supply-chain policy and its comment-spoof negative fixture must reject any publish job that does not depend exactly on both verify and recovery.

findings.attackPath: An image containing a known HIGH or CRITICAL runtime vulnerability could pass the release gate solely because the vulnerability had no upstream fix.
findings.affectedInvariant: The production vulnerability gate must reject every detected HIGH or CRITICAL runtime finding regardless of fix availability.
findings.evidence: The former Trivy step set ignore-unfixed: true; the remediated effective step sets ignore-unfixed: false.
findings.verificationRequirement: The permanent supply-chain policy must parse the effective named Trivy step and reject missing, duplicated, commented or true ignore-unfixed values.

reviewNotes: Pull-request, weekly and manual triggers; read-only permissions; non-cancelling concurrency; exact-head checkout; pinned actions; governed recovery authority; exact migration-image identity; bounded RPO/RTO inputs; PostgreSQL and Redis restore; and always-uploaded evidence were reviewed.
No confirmed defect was found in this file; the remaining staging and production-host activation boundary is recorded as residual risk rather than represented as completed.

Unconditional pull-request and main-push triggers, concurrency, read-only permissions, pinned service images and actions, exact-head verification, bounded test credentials, production environment validation, canonical migrations, exact build, governed browsers, unchanged-checkout verification and failure evidence were reviewed.
The incomplete path allowlist was removed so changes in shared runtime and security authorities cannot silently bypass the public Browser Golden Path.

findings.attackPath: A pull request changing shared code outside the former path allowlist, including src/lib authorities or src/proxy.ts, could alter production browser behavior without running the Chromium and Firefox gate.
findings.affectedInvariant: Every pull request and main push must execute the public production Browser Golden Path regardless of which tracked source path changed.
findings.evidence: The former pull_request and push triggers used a partial paths list that omitted shared runtime and security sources; the remediated triggers have no paths filter.
findings.verificationRequirement: Workflow policy and exact-head GitHub Actions evidence must demonstrate that the Browser Golden Path is not conditionally excluded by a path allowlist.

reviewNotes: Main, pull-request, daily and manual triggers; read-only permissions; exact-head full-history checkout; disabled credential persistence; pinned actions; permanent secret authority and tests; exact evidence SHA propagation; and always-uploaded redacted evidence were reviewed.
No confirmed defect was found in this file; baseline identity correctness and scanner implementation remain governed by their own pending semantic-review paths.

Retired-script fail-closed behavior, mutable installer rejection, production documentation constraints, environment-template completeness, exact Node/npm/systemd contracts, clean candidate binding, immutable build identity, Compose/public inputs, container trigger coverage, readiness probes and production-verification delegation were reviewed line by line.

The authority now parses the effective publish job and named Trivy step to require recovery before publication and reject unfixed HIGH or CRITICAL findings; negative tests include misleading comments so substring-only enforcement cannot pass.
